clue.text: Facing work, attitudinise about it

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a work

indicators.note: about means going round, so the posing word is wrapped around the next piece

parts.note: to attitudinise is to strike a pose
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confronting a job strikes an affected posture over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things facing each other sit on contrary sides, which is the adjective's sense here.

clue.text: Test an alternative to wood

parts.note: OR is the word that introduces an alternative
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: An examination of a substitute material for timber.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is softwood planking, a term less familiar outside Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe trial or test of endurance is called this.

clue.text: Where a farmer may go to sow

definitions.text: Where a farmer may go to sow

parts.words: Where a farmer may go to sow
parts.note: sow reads as planting seed, but it is the female pig, so the farmer heads for the pig's pen

explanation.surface: A farmer setting off to plant a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen where pigs, including a sow, are kept.

clue.text: Payment for clerical work

parts.note: clerical suggests office filing, but here it means work done by a cleric, whose salary has its own name

explanation.surface: Wages for office administration.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed salary, especially one paid to a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Draws certain items of attire

definitions.meaning: neckwear worn with a shirt collar

explanation.surface: A tailor sketching garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Level results in sport are draws, and neckwear knotted at the collar is the clothing sense.

clue.text: The joiner finding both the British and French deep

parts.note: the deep in English is the sea
the French word for the sea is mer

explanation.surface: A carpenter discovering the ocean in both Britain and France.
explanation.walkthrough: One 'deep' serves twice: in English it is SEA, in French MER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who stitches pieces together with seams is a joiner of a kind; it is also a cricket bowler.

clue.text: Rise, having only eaten a meal starter perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter, here of meal

explanation.surface: Someone getting up from the table having eaten only the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges EATEN plus A plus M (the starter of 'meal'); 'only' merely stresses that just the first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or spring forth, as a rumour or smell rises from a source.

clue.text: Defective hearing

parts.note: hearing suggests the ears, but here it is a court hearing that is flawed in law

explanation.surface: A complaint about poor ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial invalidated by a procedural error is a hearing that legally fails.

clue.text: Recall soldiers and possibly arm

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
an arm is an example of a limb, or member

explanation.surface: Bring back the troops and perhaps equip them.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back to mind.

clue.text: Got dried out, though very weary

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone got thoroughly dry yet stayed exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being utterly exhausted is the idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Healing agent always incorporated in herbal samples

indicators.note: incorporated in means the answer is contained within the following words

explanation.surface: A soothing remedy is always included in samples of herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'always' adds only to the surface; the answer runs across 'herbal samples'.
explanation.definitionFit: A resinous soothing ointment used medicinally.

clue.text: Gets in a bad state — such a bloomer

indicators.note: being in a bad state means disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone gets flustered over an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it means a flowering plant: GENISTA is broom.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of yellow-flowered shrubs, the brooms, so a flowering plant.

clue.text: Song setting a conservative body on edge

parts.note: taken as written
NT is the National Trust, a British organisation conserving historic places
a hem is the edge of a garment

explanation.surface: A tune that makes a Tory group nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: A national or choral song of praise.

clue.text: The weight of silver taken in last month's drive

indicators.note: taken in means one piece is absorbed inside another

parts.note: DEC is short for December, the last month
to ram is to drive forcibly
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silver ore weighed during a December push.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of mass equal to ten grams.

clue.text: Counting as influential

definitions.meaning: enumerating, as a bank teller does

explanation.surface: Numbering things as an important task.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting votes is one sense; a striking, effective argument is the other.

clue.text: This is a stick-up!

parts.note: a robber's cry, but read literally it is something that sticks things up

explanation.surface: An armed robber announcing a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky strip used to fix things to surfaces.

clue.text: Splashdown!

parts.note: suggests a spacecraft landing at sea, but read as water splashing downwards it is a great waterfall

explanation.surface: A space capsule hitting the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A large steep waterfall, where water crashes down.

clue.text: Scoffing about a Greek character — nothing can sting one

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scoffing word surrounds the rest

parts.note: scoffing at something is treating it with scorn
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Mocking a Greek figure, who cannot be hurt by anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'one [that] can sting'.
explanation.definitionFit: An arachnid with a venomous tail, a creature that can sting.

clue.text: They are charged for current usage

definitions.text: They are charged for current usage

parts.words: They are charged for current usage
parts.note: charged suggests a fee for present use, but it means filled with electricity to supply electric current

explanation.surface: Customers billed for what they use today.
explanation.definitionFit: Rechargeable batteries store electric charge to supply power.

clue.text: Tycoon requiring new gateman

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A business mogul needs a fresh doorkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy, powerful industrialist.

clue.text: Note: goes for profit

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
goes means takes a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: A memo says it is heading off for gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns on an investment are the profits it yields.

clue.text: Fall after heartless fool causes injury

indicators.note: after places the falling word behind the trimmed fool
heartless means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool
rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: A tumble following a callous idiot's blunder leads to hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle A from SAP to leave SP.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrenched ligament is a common injury.

clue.text: All rounder in the field?

parts.note: suggests a cricketer good at everything, but it is something perfectly round, and also a field of activity

explanation.surface: A versatile cricketer out fielding.
explanation.definitionFit: A globe is round all over, and the word also means a domain of activity or influence.

clue.text: Arranging a grant — or too proud?

indicators.note: arranging means putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Is organising a funding award something done with conceit?
explanation.definitionFit: Haughty and overbearing, having an exaggerated sense of self-importance.

clue.text: Don't go to bed early when it's close

explanation.surface: Advice to keep late hours on a nearly finished night.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying awake late is one phrasal sense; plugging or blocking a gap is the other.

clue.text: Put up with a churlish individual

explanation.surface: Tolerating a rude person.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate is one sense; a gruff, ill-mannered person is the other.

clue.text: Giving a punch in return is brutal

indicators.note: in return reads the pieces backwards, coming back the other way

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hitting back is savage behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' acts on the whole run of pieces, not just the punch; the surface hides that 'in' is fodder rather than part of the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Beastly, purely physical and savage is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Press for a reduction

definitions.meaning: ironing a garment, cryptically taking the creases out

explanation.surface: Lobbying to bring something down.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironing takes creases out, so 'Press' can be read as de-crease, while the plain sense of the answer is a cut or lowering.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing removes the creases, a whimsical sense, while a lessening in amount is the ordinary noun.

clue.text: Enters uncertainly, being more nervous

indicators.note: uncertainly suggests the letters are in an unsettled order

explanation.surface: Someone comes in hesitantly, growing more anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: More taut and anxious, the comparative of an adjective for strain.

clue.text: Imposing appearance before sound sense

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: sound means the following word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: taken as written for its spoken form

explanation.surface: An impressive look comes ahead of solid judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: A commanding bearing that makes an impression on others.
